aiConsent.title: AI features send messages off your device
aiConsent.body:
Chatterbox encrypts your messages so only you and the other person can read them. AI is the one exception.

To summarise, translate or transcribe, the selected messages are decrypted on this device and sent to our server and its AI provider. They are sent to produce your result, not to train anything — but in transit and in processing they are not end-to-end encrypted.

Everything else stays encrypted: messages you don't run AI on, your shared lists.

You can turn this off at any time in Profile.
aiConsent.settingsOn: Allowed — selected messages are sent off this device when you use AI.
aiConsent.settingsOff: Off — nothing is sent. You'll be asked before any AI feature runs.
aiConsent.turnedOff: AI features turned off on this device

linkPreview.settingsOn: On — when you send a link, this device fetches its title and image once and encrypts them into the message. The person you send it to never asks our server about the link.
linkPreview.settingsOff: Off — links you send stay plain links, and our server is never told about them.

tutorial.welcomeBody: Let's take a quick tour of the essentials — it only takes a few taps.
tutorial.chatsBody: All your conversations live in the Chats tab. Unread messages show a badge there.
tutorial.newChatBody: Tap the + in Chats to send someone an invite link, or open one they sent you.
tutorial.composerBody: In a chat you can send photos, files, voice notes and GIFs, reply or @mention, and even schedule a message for later.
tutorial.spacesBody: Open a chat's menu for the media gallery and collaborative lists — both end-to-end encrypted, like the messages.
tutorial.callsBody: Call anyone right from the chat — one tap for voice, one for video.
tutorial.profileBody: Set your name, theme, language and privacy here — and replay this tour anytime.
tutorial.doneBody: That's the tour. You can replay it whenever you like from your profile.
tutorial.settingsDescription: New here? Take the guided tour of Chatterbox.

recovery.superseded: This device's encryption key was replaced from another device, so messages sent to you since then can't be opened here. Sending still works. Enter the recovery phrase from that other device below to read the rest.
recovery.alreadyRevealed: You've already saved your recovery phrase on this device. For your security it won't be shown again — if you still have it, keep it somewhere safe. If you lost it, this device keeps working normally; you'll only need it to restore old messages on a different device.
recovery.restoreFirst: This device doesn't have your account's encryption key yet, so there's no phrase to show — the one you want was saved on your other device. Enter it below to restore your message history. Once that's done, this phrase becomes available here too.
recovery.unavailable: We couldn't check this device's encryption status, so the phrase isn't being shown yet — revealing it now could overwrite a key you may still need. Check your connection and come back.
recovery.backUp: Back up the key that protects your messages. Anyone who sees this phrase can read your message history, so only reveal it somewhere private.
recovery.restoreBody: Entering a previously saved recovery phrase replaces this device's key, so it can decrypt messages sealed to that phrase.
recovery.prepareFailed: We couldn't prepare your recovery phrase just now. Your messages are unaffected — you can try again any time from Settings.
recovery.whatItDoes: This phrase can restore your encrypted message history if you ever reinstall the app or switch devices. Anyone who has it can read your messages, so write it down and keep it somewhere private — it will not be shown again.
recovery.restoredBody: Reopen your chats to see any messages that couldn't be decrypted before.
recovery.invalidBody: Check that all 24 words are spelled correctly and in order, then try again.
recovery.unverifiableBody: We couldn't reach the server to confirm this phrase belongs to your account, so nothing has been changed. Check your connection and try again.
recovery.publishFailedBody: Your phrase was correct, but we couldn't save the change. Nothing has been changed on this device — check your connection and try again.
recovery.mismatchTitle: This phrase isn't the key on file
recovery.mismatchBody:
It may be from an older device, in which case restoring it is exactly what you want — it will bring back messages this device cannot read.

Your account will go back to using that older key. Anything sealed to the current key since then will stop being readable here, and your other devices will need this same phrase.
